To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the absorption and fluorescence of nucleic acids can be used to quantify nucleic acids, and that (2) the fluorescence of ethidium bromides and Hoechst 33,258 is quenched by nucleic acids, but that of PicoGreen is enhanced by nucleic acids.
the PicoGreen dsDNA quantitation assay is more sensitive and accurate than the Hoechst 33358 assay, and that the ethidium bromine assay is the most accurate of all three assays.
The PicoGreen assay is a highly sensitive and specific method for measuring DNA and RNA concentrations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and more sensitive methods for the determination of nucleic acids.
the development of new analytical methods for the detection of trace amounts of nucleic acids in complex biological samples.
the development and application of novel fluorescence-based techniques for nucleic acid quantitation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PicoGreen is the most sensitive and most accurate assay, and that Hoechst 33342 is the second most sensitive assay.
the use of the fluorescence techniques, especially PicoGreen, is the most sensitive method for the quantitation of DNA and/or RNA.
PicoGreen is the method of choice for quantitation of DNA and that Hoechst 33342 and ethidium brombe should be avoided.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

absorbance at 260nm, ethidium, Hoechst and PicoGreen can be used to quantify DNA, but that absorbance at260nm and Hoechst can be used to quantitate RNA, while the other two methods cannot be used to quantitatively assess RNA.
the PicoGreen assay is the most sensitive and reliable method for DNA quantitation, while the Hoechst 33,258 assay is the most reliable method for RNA quantitation.

The main takeaway from our work is that
PicoGreen is a highly sensitive and specific fluorescent dye for the quantitation of DNA and that it is suitable for use with as little as 25 pg/ml DNA.
PicoGreen is the best method for quantifying small amounts of DNA and RNA.
the use of a single method for quantitation of DNA and of RNA can result in errors that are unacceptable for many applications.
